authority_name: Public Information Officer (PIO) of the concerned Public Authority
authority_short: PIO / First Appellate Authority / Central Information Commission
description: RTI Applications under the Right to Information Act, 2005 are filed in a three-tier system: first to the designated PIO of the public authority, then to the First Appellate Authority within that department if unsatisfied, and finally to the Central Information Commission (for central public authorities) or State Information Commission (for state public authorities) as a second appeal.

filing_tiers.name: Public Information Officer (PIO)
filing_tiers.description: File your RTI application directly to the PIO of the specific public authority (e.g., Ministry of Railways, Municipal Corporation). Every public authority under RTI Act 2005 must designate a PIO.
filing_tiers.deadline_to_respond: 30 days (10 days if life/liberty is involved — RTI Act 2005, Section 7)
filing_tiers.how_to_file: In writing (physical / postal) or online via RTI Online portal for central govt authorities

filing_tiers.name: First Appellate Authority (FAA)
filing_tiers.description: If PIO denies information or does not reply within 30 days, appeal to the First Appellate Authority within the same public authority.
filing_tiers.deadline_to_file: Within 30 days of receiving PIO response (or 30 days after deadline if no response)

filing_tiers.name: Central / State Information Commission
filing_tiers.description: Second and final appeal to the CIC (central authorities) or SIC (state authorities). Can award penalties up to ₹25,000 on errant PIOs.
filing_tiers.note: State-specific SIC portals vary by state — check your state government website

portal_scope: Central Government public authorities only. For state authorities, file with the respective state RTI portal or physically.

payment_methods_central: Online payment via RTI Online portal
fee.fee_exemption: Persons below poverty line (BPL) are exempt from fee — attach BPL card copy
fee.state_fees: needs_verification — state RTI fees vary; most states charge ₹10–₹50
fee.source: RTI Act 2005, Section 6(1) and RTI (Regulation of Fee and Cost) Rules, 2005

required_documents: Written RTI application (in English, Hindi, or official language of the state)
Applicant name, address, and contact details
Application fee (Demand Draft / IPO / postal order / online payment)
BPL card copy (if claiming fee exemption)
response_timeline: 30 days from receipt by PIO (10 days if the matter involves life or liberty)
important_notes: RTI does not apply to certain exempt organisations listed in the Second Schedule of the RTI Act (e.g., Intelligence Bureau, RAW).
You do not need to give any reason for seeking information.
Information that would endanger national security or privacy of a third party may be withheld under Sections 8 and 9.
If your PIO is in a central government ministry, use the RTI Online portal for fastest processing.
eligibility_prerequisites: Must be a Citizen of India (Section 3, Right to Information Act 2005).
Public authority must fall under the definition of Section 2(h) of the RTI Act.
Information sought must exist in material record format (documents, memos, emails, records, orders) and not fall under exemptions in Section 8 or 9.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Identify Public Authority and PIO
step_by_step_procedure.description: Determine the exact department, ministry, or public authority that holds the required records and locate their designated Public Information Officer (PIO/CPIO).

step_by_step_procedure.title: Draft Specific, Point-Wise Questions
step_by_step_procedure.description: Write clear, numbered queries requesting specific documents or records. Avoid seeking opinions, interpretations, or legal justifications.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Pay the Statutory Application Fee
step_by_step_procedure.description: Attach the ₹10 fee via IPO, demand draft, banker's cheque, or online payment. If Below Poverty Line (BPL), attach a valid BPL card copy for full fee exemption.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Submit Application and Retain Tracking Proof
step_by_step_procedure.description: Submit online via RTI Online portal (for central ministries) or send by Registered Post with Acknowledgement Due (RPAD) / Speed Post. Keep the postal receipt and tracking number.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Statutory Response Period
step_by_step_procedure.description: PIO must provide information or reject with reasons within 30 days of receipt (within 48 hours if life and liberty of a person is involved).

step_by_step_procedure.title: File First Appeal (if necessary)
step_by_step_procedure.description: If no reply is received within 30 days or information is unsatisfactory, file a First Appeal with the First Appellate Authority (FAA) within 30 days.

step_by_step_procedure.title: File Second Appeal with Information Commission
step_by_step_procedure.description: If FAA fails to decide or gives an adverse order, file a Second Appeal with the Central Information Commission (CIC) or State Information Commission (SIC) within 90 days.

common_mistakes: Asking questions seeking opinions, justifications ('Why did you...'), or legal advice instead of existing material records.
Submitting applications meant for State Government departments on the Central Government rtionline.gov.in portal.
Failing to retain the postal registration receipt, acknowledgment card, and a signed photocopy of the application.
Exceeding reasonable bounds with overly voluminous or 30-year-old unindexed requests.
Forgetting to enclose fee proof or attaching invalid non-statutory payment instruments.
checklist: Application is clearly addressed to the Public Information Officer (PIO/CPIO)
Queries are numbered, factual, and request existing material records
Applicant name, postal address, and contact information are fully filled
Statutory fee of ₹10 attached (or BPL card copy enclosed for exemption)
Application is dated and signed by the citizen
Duplicate copy and postal/online acknowledgment preserved
source_ref: Right to Information Act 2005 (Act 22 of 2005); RTI (Regulation of Fee and Cost) Rules 2005; CIC website cic.gov.in

authority_short: District / State / National Consumer Commission (DCDRC / SCDRC / NCDRC)
description: Consumer complaints under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 are filed with the Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions, which operate at three levels based on the value of the goods/services plus compensation sought. The e-Daakhil portal (edaakhil.nic.in) enables online filing for all three tiers.

filing_tiers.note: File at the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in your district

filing_tiers.jurisdiction: Claims above ₹50 lakh up to ₹2 crore
filing_tiers.note: File at the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in your state capital

filing_tiers.address: National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Upbhokta Nyay Bhawan, F-Block, GPO Complex, INA, New Delhi — 110 023
filing_tiers.note: Can also be filed online via e-Daakhil portal

portal_name: e-Daakhil (National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission — official portal)
portal_scope: All three tiers (District, State, National). Allows online complaint filing, tracking, and hearing scheduling.

fee.structure: Fee is based on the value of goods/services and compensation claimed
fee.payment_online: Via e-Daakhil portal using net banking / UPI / debit card
fee.payment_offline: Demand Draft in favour of the respective Commission
fee.source: Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020 — Schedule of Fees

required_documents: Consumer complaint form (can be submitted via e-Daakhil portal)
Purchase invoice / receipt / contract / service agreement (proof of transaction)
Evidence of defect/deficiency (photos, test reports, correspondence with seller/company)
Copy of legal notice sent to the opposite party (if sent)
Identity and address proof of complainant
response_timeline: Opposite party must file response within 30 days; Commission aims to dispose cases within 3 months (5 months where laboratory testing required) — Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 38
legal_basis: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Act 35 of 2019); Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020
important_notes: You can file online without a lawyer — the process is designed to be citizen-accessible.
Limitation period: complaint must be filed within 2 years of the cause of action (defect/deficiency).
Mediation is mandatory at the first stage — the Commission will refer to mediation if both parties agree.
Legal notice to the opposite party before filing is advisable but not mandatory.
eligibility_prerequisites: Must be a 'Consumer' under Section 2(7) of Consumer Protection Act 2019 (bought goods or hired services for personal use/consideration, not for resale or commercial purpose).
Must have an actionable grievance (defect in goods, deficiency in service, unfair trade practice, or misleading advertisement).
Filing must be within the 2-year statutory limitation period from the date the cause of action arose (Section 69).

step_by_step_procedure.title: Serve Informal Grievance or Legal Notice
step_by_step_procedure.description: Send a formal notice or email to the seller/service provider stating the defect/deficiency and providing 15 days to resolve or refund.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Assemble Transaction and Defect Evidence
step_by_step_procedure.description: Collect tax invoice, proof of payment, warranty card, product photos, job cards, service communications, and seller's rejection/silence.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Determine Pecuniary and Territorial Commission
step_by_step_procedure.description: Calculate total value of goods/services paid plus compensation: District Commission (up to ₹50 Lakh), State Commission (₹50 Lakh to ₹2 Crore), National Commission (>₹2 Crore). File where you reside or where seller has office.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Draft Complaint Petition and Verification Affidavit
step_by_step_procedure.description: Draft petition with indexed chronology of events, clear prayer/relief sought, and an affidavit affirming the contents on oath.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Submit Online via e-Daakhil Portal or Offline
step_by_step_procedure.description: Register on edaakhil.nic.in, upload complaint petition, supporting annexures, and pay the prescribed fee online. Physical filing at the Commission registry is also permitted.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Admission and Notice to Opposite Party
step_by_step_procedure.description: Commission examines admissibility within 21 days. Once admitted, notice is issued to the opposite party to submit a written reply within 30 days.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Hearing or Mediation and Final Order
step_by_step_procedure.description: Parties may opt for consumer mediation cell for speedy settlement. Otherwise, summary hearings proceed on affidavits without requiring lengthy court trials.

common_mistakes: Filing after the 2-year limitation period without an application for condonation of delay explaining the cause.
Purchasing goods for commercial resale or industrial enterprise, which falls outside consumer court protection.
Filing in the incorrect commission tier by calculating only compensation rather than total value of goods/services plus compensation.
Omitting the manufacturer as a necessary party when defect is inherent to the product rather than dealer fault.
Failing to produce concrete documentary evidence (invoice, warranty, or written rejection).
checklist: Complaint petition with indexed list of dates and events
Signed and notarised verification affidavit
Original/copy of tax invoice or booking receipt
Proof of consideration paid (bank statement / UPI / card receipt)
Photographs / test reports / technical expert opinion of defect (if applicable)
Copy of notice sent to seller/service provider with proof of delivery
Proof of payment of statutory filing fee under 2020 Rules
source_ref: Consumer Protection Act 2019, Sections 34–59; Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules 2020; e-Daakhil portal edaakhil.nic.in

authority_name: No Central Government Portal — Served Directly to Opposite Party
description: A legal demand notice is served directly to the opposite party — it is not filed with any government portal. It is a formal written communication before initiating legal proceedings. If the matter is not resolved after the notice, the next step is filing a civil suit in the appropriate Civil Court.

filing_tiers.name: Serve notice to opposite party
filing_tiers.description: Send via Registered Post with Acknowledgement Due (RPAD) to the opposite party's last known address. Keep the postal receipt and returned acknowledgement card as proof of service.
alternatives: Email (if service via email is agreed or can be proven)

filing_tiers.name: File civil suit in Civil Court
filing_tiers.description: If the opposite party does not respond or does not comply within the notice period, file a civil suit. Court depends on jurisdiction and claim amount.

jurisdiction.money_claims_up_to: needs_verification — varies by state. Generally: District Munsiff/Civil Judge (Junior Division) courts for smaller claims; District Court for larger.
jurisdiction.note: Court fees are state-specific under the respective State Court Fees Acts — check your state's court fee schedule.

portal_name: No portal — physical or postal service only
portal_scope: Not applicable. For landlord-tenant disputes in some states, Rent Authority portals may exist — needs_verification by state.

fee.notice_sending_fee: India Post RPAD: approximately ₹35–₹80 depending on weight and city (check indiapost.gov.in for current rates)
fee.court_filing_fee: needs_verification — court fees are governed by the Court Fees Act 1870 and respective State Court Fees Acts; they vary by claim value and state
fee.lawyer_fees: Optional — not required for sending a legal notice, but recommended for complex disputes
fee.source: India Post rate card; Court Fees Act 1870 (as amended by states)

required_documents: Legal demand notice (addressed to opposite party, signed by sender)
Supporting evidence of the dispute (e.g., rent receipts, original agreement, photographs, correspondence)
Copy of relevant agreements (lease/rent agreement, service contract, purchase invoice)
response_timeline: Typically 15–30 days notice period is given in the notice itself. No statutory deadline — set by sender.
legal_basis: Legal notices are governed by the substantive law underlying the dispute (e.g., Transfer of Property Act 1882 for landlord-tenant; Contract Act 1872 for contract disputes; Code of Civil Procedure 1908 for civil suits)
important_notes: A legal notice is not mandatory before filing a civil suit (except in certain specific cases like defamation under Section 80 CPC, or suits against government).
Sending a notice via RPAD creates a legal presumption of service — keep the tracking proof.
For landlord-tenant disputes: many states have Rent Control Acts with dedicated Rent Tribunals — check your state's rent law.
Court fees for civil suits are state-specific and cannot be stated without knowing your state — consult your state court fee schedule or a local lawyer.
eligibility_prerequisites: Any individual, citizen, or entity having an unfulfilled contractual obligation, tenancy violation, property dispute, or unpaid dues.
Clear legal grievance supported by written or material evidence (agreement, receipts, correspondence).
Exact name and identifiable address of the opposite party.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Review Legal Grounds and Contract Terms
step_by_step_procedure.description: Examine the underlying agreement (e.g. lease agreement, invoice, employment letter) and compute exact claim amount and interest if legally applicable.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Draft the Demand Notice with Clear Specifics
step_by_step_procedure.description: Set out the facts chronologically, state the exact breach/default, specify the exact monetary demand or required action, and give a clear compliance period (typically 15 to 30 days).

step_by_step_procedure.title: Date and Execute the Notice
step_by_step_procedure.description: Sign the notice. Retain an identical signed office copy along with all attached annexures and supporting documents.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Dispatch via Registered Post (RPAD) or Speed Post
step_by_step_procedure.description: Send the notice via India Post Registered Post with Acknowledgement Due (RPAD) or Speed Post with delivery tracking. You may also email a scanned copy concurrently.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Track Consignment and Archive Service Proof
step_by_step_procedure.description: Download the official delivery confirmation from indiapost.gov.in and store the original postal receipt and signed green RPAD acknowledgment card securely in LEXIS Vault.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Await Notice Expiry and Evaluate Response
step_by_step_procedure.description: Allow the full statutory or specified notice period (e.g. 15 or 30 days) from the date of confirmed delivery for the opposite party to comply or respond.

step_by_step_procedure.title: Initiate Litigation (if unresolved)
step_by_step_procedure.description: If the demand is rejected or ignored, proceed to file a civil suit in the competent Civil Court or file an application before the relevant Rent/Labour Tribunal.

common_mistakes: Sending only by regular unrecorded post or instant messenger without retaining legally admissible proof of delivery.
Using aggressive, defamatory, or criminal threats in a matter that is purely civil or contractual.
Failing to specify a definitive deadline for compliance or quoting ambiguous, unsubstantiated claim amounts.
Failing to preserve the postal booking receipt, postal tracking printout, and signed RPAD card.
Overlooking specific statutory notice periods (e.g., Section 80 CPC requires mandatory 2-month notice before suing Government; Section 138 NI Act requires 15-day notice within 30 days of memo).
checklist: Notice is legibly addressed to the full legal name and current address of opposite party
Chronological statement of facts and legal basis clearly articulated
Specific demand (remedy/sum) clearly stated
Clear time period for compliance specified (15, 30, or 60 days)
Notice dated and signed by sender or legal representative
Dispatched via India Post RPAD / Speed Post with postal receipt securely preserved
Delivery tracking report downloaded and stored
source_ref: Transfer of Property Act 1882; Indian Contract Act 1872; Code of Civil Procedure 1908; Court Fees Act 1870
